title: The present with bi- and the day

blocks.text: You used Egyptian verbs as phrases up to here: baštaġal, bitištaġal ēh?, batʿallim. In this unit you understand the mechanism: the present Egyptian forms by adding b- to the imperfect, and with this only tool tell your day, your habits and what you are doing now. You also learn the time, days of the week and frequency adverbs. Six weeks, in parallel with B1-06 and B1-07.

rows: 8–9 hours · six weeks (weeks 107–112), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, a tutor or Egyptian conversation partner, tutor recordings on the phone
Targets. At the end of the unit you know:
1. to combine the most common, regular and irregular Egyptian verbs at present;
2. use the present with b- for current habits and actions;
3. To deny the present with but...-š and with miš;
4. say and ask the time and days of the week;
5. Tell your day, like, and ask about the other guys.
Six-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week).
To Tuesday's tandem Šarīf and Luke tell their days.

Exclamation of surprise or fear (Lett. "Protector!" is a name of God. zākir (for school); daras is a subject at the university.

The Egyptian verb has two main times, such as the fuṣḥā: the perfect (EGY-04) and the imperfect. The simple imperfect, without prefixes, is used after the modal verbs and in some buildings (EGY-08: ʿāyiz arūḥ I want to go. lāzim you have to have breakfast. With the prefix b- becomes the present , which covers two Italian meanings:

rows: I'm talking to a friend right now.

blocks.text: general truth il-maṣriyyīn biyḥibbu š-šāy. Egyptians love tea. The fuṣḥā Compared. The present Egyptian corresponds to the imperfect indicative of the fuṣḥā: baktib = ⁧أَكْتُبُ⁩ , biyiktib = ⁧يَكْتُبُ⁩ . The b- does not have equivalent: it is one of the first things that make a dialect recognize (in Levante we also use b-, in the Gulf no). Action in progress with emphasis. To say "I'm doing it right, I'm continuing to do it" is used ʿammāl + present: ʿammāl azākir min iṣ-ṣubḥ I've been studying since this morning. Just recognize him.
The present is formed with b- + prefix of the imperfect + root + suffix . In front of ni-, ti-, yi- the b- takes one i (bi-).

The vowel. Each verb has its own vowel (i) a) between the second and third radical: yiktib, but yišrab. Learn the verb with its imperfect, as in fuṣḥā. inta and hiyya have the same shape (bitiktib): decides the context. Verbs with more than three letters (from derived forms): bakallim batʿallim, bititʿallim; baštaġal, bitištaġal. Here the i of the prefix often falls before a double consonant or group (bitkallim).

rows: yuʾʿud Sit down; Staying in the room

blocks.text: Three guys. 1. Concave verbs (rūḥ, nām): the long vowel remains, the prefix loses i (bitrūḥ). 2. Words ending in vowel (yigi, yimši, yiṣḥa): the final vowel falls (biyimšu). 3. yākul and yāḫud: the root initial hamza becomes ā (fuṣḥā ⁧يَأْكُلُ⁩ , ⁧يَأْخُذُ⁩ ).

ana miš baštaġal bukra, ana fi agāza.

blocks.text: Watch the sounds. ma-bitrūḥš "Do not go," ma-binnāmš We don't sleep, ma-biyišrabūš They do not drink: before -š the final vowel -u becomes long (-ūš) and the -i becomes -īš: ma-bitiktibīš Do not write (f.)
What time? ⁧؟⁩ … ⁧الساعة كام⁩ is-sāʿa kām…?

The hour shall use the numbers "Inner" (talāta, arbaʿa, tamanya), not the short forms of EGY-02. 1 is is-sāʿa waḥda; 12 is-sāʿa itnāšar. To distinguish morning and evening: is-sāʿa sabʿa ṣ-ṣubḥ 7:00 a.m., is-sāʿa sabʿa bi-l-lēl Seven in the evening. Tilt is a third of twenty minutes: it's a typically Egyptian way of saying the time. You also feel tamanya w-ʿišrīn.

Saturday is-sabt today · tomorrow · yesterday in-naharda · bukra · imbāriḥ
The weekend in Egypt is Friday and, for many, Saturday. Sunday is a business day. The frequency.
ʿumri ma- ... never in my life... ʿumri ma-šuft il-Aʾṣur I've never seen Luxor. with the present: ʿumri ma-bašrab ʾahwa bi-l-lēl I never drink coffee in the evening.

The prefix. Pronouncing the b- attached to the verb, without pauses: biyiktib, not bi yiktib. In the quick biyi-talk it shortens: listen to how the tutor pronounces it and imitate it. Remember that Cairo is always ba-: baktib. Vowels falling. biyāklu, biyāḫdu: u of yākul It falls in front of -u. bitkallim, bitzākir: the i of the prefix falls. Shadowing. 1. My day (session). Tell the tutor about your day, like, in two minutes: wake up, breakfast, work, Meals, evening. The tutor interrupts you with questions (is-sāʿa kām? w-baʿdēn? fēn?).
2. Interview. Ask the tutor ten questions about his day and his habits, with at least three adverbs of different frequency. Then report in third person (biyiṣḥa…, biyrūḥ…).
3. On the phone. The tutor calls you at a time of day: answer by saying what you are doing (ana bazākir, ana fi l-meter, ana bākul...) and set an hour to hear from you.
